title.narrative: Higher Education in the Pacific Investment Program - Tranche 2

description.narrative: Project 2 (with additional financing) will support the expansion of the University of the South Pacific (USP) regional campus in Solomon Islands to a new location in Honiara, at the King George VI School grounds, about 4 kilometers east of the existing campus. The scope of Project 2 includes (i) construction of classrooms, an ICT studio, science laboratories, faculty offices, administrative facilities, and a clean energy component supporting a solar photo-voltaic system; (ii) enhancement of ICT-based education; (iii) improvement of student support services; (iv) strengthening of USP governance and management; and (v) strengthening project management capacity of USP staff who will be involved in project implementation. Project 2 will enable the USP regional campus in Solomon Islands to accommodate an increasing demand for higher education, improve the quality of education through the use of ICT and adoption of distance flexible learning, and increase course offerings especially in the field of public health which is the anchor program for the campus. It will also help improve USP student services through provision of pre-enrollment information and career counseling, strengthening governance and management capacity of USP (improved data collection and analysis of USP activities and human resources), and strengthening capacity of USP personnel to effectively manage project activities.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Improved USP student services Indicator: At least 50% of USP graduates, including at least 55% of the female graduates, receive support from newly established job search or job counseling services by 2020 Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved. 100% of students, including females receive job counselling services. Data Source: Graduate destination and program experience surveys

Output: Improved USP student services Indicator: The rate of satisfaction with orientation programs reaches at least 70% by 2018 and 80% by 2020 among entering students (new surveys to be undertaken) Achievement: 95 Progress/Status: Achieved. 95% of students were satisfied with orientation programs in 2018 and 2020. Data Source: Graduate destination and program experience surveys

Output: Improved USP student services Indicator: The rate of satisfaction with orientation programs reaches at least 80% by 2020 among entering students (new surveys to be undertaken) Data Source: Graduate destination and program experience surveys Actual value:

Output: Regional campus in Solomon Islands strengthened Indicator: At least 6 new classrooms and learning related facilities including separate sanitation facilities operate with adequate ICT equipment for mixed modes of teaching including DFL by 2025 Achievement: 100% Progress/Status: The contract was awarded to the first-ranked firm on 20 February 2020. Disbursement for the advance payment was made in Q2 2020. Due to the COVID-19 outbreak and resulting travel bans in the Solomon Islands, mobilization was moved a number of times initially from May 2020 to August 2020, then January 2021, and finally to April 2021. The contractor mobilized to the Solomon Islands on 5 April 2021, and construction works commenced in May 2021. Campus construction works were substantially completed by 22 December 2023, and handover was completed in January 2024. Campus inauguration was held on 3 October 2024. Data Source: USP official statistics
Actual value: 100%

Output: Regional campus in Solomon Islands strengthened Indicator: Clean energy sources connected to meet 75% of projected campus power needs Achievement: 100% Progress/Status: The solar PV system has been installed and in operation since 22 December 2023. Data Source: Project progress reports Actual value: 100%

Output: USP governance and management strengthened Indicator: Females will hold 20% of management-level positions by 2020 (0% in 2016) Achievement: 40 Progress/Status: Females held 40% of management-level positions at USP Solomon Islands Campus by 2024. Data Source: Internal audit reports
Output: ICT-based education in Solomon Islands enhanced Indicator: with at least 50% of ICT-based DFL users being female (baseline 41% in 2015) Achievement: 43 Data Source: USP official statistics

Output: USP governance and management strengthened Indicator: 80% of internal audit report recommendations are complied with by 2020 (baseline 50% in 2014) Achievement: 86 Progress/Status: 86% of internal audit recommendations for USP Solomon Islands were complied with by 2020. Data Source: USP management reports

Output: ICT-based education in Solomon Islands enhanced Indicator: At least 15% of Solomon Island students use ICT-based mode for DFL by 2025 (baseline 9% in 2016), with at least 50% of ICT-based DFL users being female (baseline 41% in 2015) Achievement: 45 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. 45% of students were enrolled in blended and online DFL education. 47% of students (versus a target of 50%) enrolled in online DFL in 2021 were female. Data Source: USP official statistics

Output: ICT-based education in Solomon Islands enhanced Indicator: Percentage of courses that utilize Moodle as a learning management system increases from 90% in 2016 to 100% by 2020 Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All course contents are provided on Moodle from 2020. Data Source: USP official statistics
